text:
Maya K: heads up — we started seeing a spike of failing external requests from edge pods in eu-west-1 around 09:12 UTC. model pull & telemetry endpoints return 503/connection refused. OpsBot alerted.
Sanjay R: can you share a sample pod + curl output?
Maya K: yep. from rtx-sidecar-5 pod: `kubectl exec -it rtx-sidecar-5 -- curl -sv https://models.redwood-internal.example.com/v1/pulls` -> TLS handshake then `* Received HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable`
Liam: I tried `tcpdump -n -i any 'port 443'` inside the pod — I can see SYNs to external IPs but replies are RST from local IP. looks like traffic is being intercepted and rejected locally.
Jun P: that's classic sidecar egress deny. our Envoy bootstrap has `egress_mode: DEFAULT_DENY` in the eu-west profile after the last rollout. Could be the sidecar filter set to only allow cluster/internal CIDRs.
Maya K: sidecar logs show `route: no cluster found for outbound https://models.redwood-internal.example.com` and `proxy error: egress policy denied`
Sanjay R: OpsBot, paste the deploy rollout for `sidecar-config` in eu-west-1 please.
OpsBot: rollout/sidecar-config eu-west-1 @ 2026-03-18T08:45:12Z (image: envoy/edge:2.3.1, config-tag: egress-default-deny) :thumbsup:
Liam: quick debug steps I ran:
```
# from noisy pod
kubectl exec -n edge rtx-sidecar-5 -- curl -v https://models.redwood-internal.example.com/v1/pulls
kubectl logs rtx-sidecar-5 -c envoy | tail -n 50
kubectl exec -n edge rtx-sidecar-5 -- iptables -t nat -L -n -v
```
Jun P: iptables likely has a REDIRECT to 15001 (Envoy). If Envoy has no egress cluster for that external host the request is dropped/503. Short term we can whitelist the models domain in the egress filter or route through our egress-gateway.
Maya K: I added `sidecar.redwood.io/allow-egress: "true"` annotation to the deployment to test -> just got green for one instance. but that's a temp workaround, not for all services.
Sanjay R: good test. Can we instead add a cluster-level egress rule: allow `models.redwood-internal.example.com` and telemetry hosts to 10.0.0.0/8 + CIDR for managed services?
Liam: adding that to the `egress-policy` map in config-server should do it. sample envoy filter we used historically:
```
- name: allow-per-host
  match: {}
  allow:
    hosts:
      - models.redwood-internal.example.com
      - telemetry.redwood-internal.example.com
```
Jun P: note: this rollout was intended to harden egress because we saw data exfil attempts last quarter. default-deny is desired, but the problem is our list excludes service discovery/managed endpoints. Need an automated test that runs after sidecar config rollouts to call our internal external endpoints.
Maya K: can we also add the NAT gateway range to the allowed outbound IP ranges? some pods expect SNAT to our NAT IP and Envoy was stripping it.
Sanjay R: yes, update the egress-gateway profile to include the NAT IP ranges and add a healthcheck in the ci/cd gating job.
OpsBot: action items created: RD-1123 add eu-west model hosts to egress allowlist; RD-1124 add NAT CIDRs to egress-gateway; RD-1125 add post-rollout smoke tests.
Maya K: assigning RD-1123 to me, RD-1124 to Jun, RD-1125 to Liam.
Liam: spin up canary with `sidecar-config:egress-allowlist-v1` and route 5% of traffic through it -> confirm model pulls stable then promote.
Jun P: I'll prepare the config diff. pro tip: include the cluster's SNI host mapping in Envoy to avoid route mismatches.
Sanjay R: thanks — let's keep the canary limited to eu-west for now. if any failures revert to `egress-default-deny` quickly.
Maya K: thanks team, patch started. will ping here when canary is live. :rocket:
